system.name: Flock
system.one_liner: a framework for deploying on-demand distributed trust across serverless functions using a NAT-independent relay for secure networking

content.subject: the two-phase TLS handshake protocol Flock's Relay uses to connect two serverless instances without exposing them to each other directly

elements.name: s1
elements.role: left serverless instance's lifeline, initiates the protocol as a serverless-to-relay connection

elements.name: Relay
elements.role: middle party run by the application provider that relays and authenticates both serverless instances

elements.name: s2
elements.role: right serverless instance's lifeline, the peer s1 wants to establish a direct secure connection with

elements.name: Invoke
elements.role: each instance's initial invocation carrying its PartyID and RelayTarget (IP, Port)

elements.name: mTLS Handshake
elements.role: mutual-TLS handshake each instance performs with the Relay to authenticate itself (S2R phase), then repeated end-to-end for S2S

elements.name: Destination
elements.role: tells the Relay which other PartyID this instance wants to connect to

elements.name: Assign
elements.role: Relay assigns one instance the TLS Server role and the other the TLS Client role

elements.name: Downgrade TLS to TCP
elements.role: each instance downgrades its authenticated TLS session to a bare TCP socket the Relay can forward

elements.name: SSL_SHUTDOWN
elements.role: signals the TLS layer is being torn down while keeping the underlying authorized socket

elements.name: Establish: s1-s2 Forwarding
elements.role: Relay begins forwarding raw bytes between the two downgraded sockets

elements.name: TLS Connection Request
elements.role: the assigned TLS Client (s2) opens a new TLS connection over the forwarded socket

elements.name: Secure connection
elements.role: the resulting end-to-end TLS session directly authenticated between s1 and s2 (S2S phase)

content.key_idea: Flock's Relay authenticates each serverless instance separately (teal S2R) before downgrading and re-forwarding their sockets so the instances complete a direct mTLS handshake (green S2S) end-to-end.
content.reading_order: top-down along the two outer lifelines (s1 left, s2 right) through the central Relay column, teal S2R steps first, green S2S steps last

summary: Flock deploys on-demand distributed trust for serverless functions using a NAT-independent relay so two serverless instances can talk securely without a direct connection. This sequence diagram walks through the Flock Relay's two-phase per-invocation protocol between client s1, the central Relay, and client s2. In the teal serverless-to-relay (S2R) phase, both instances invoke with a PartyID and RelayTarget, mutually-TLS-handshake with the Relay, and declare their Destination; the Relay assigns one instance the TLS Server role and the other TLS Client. Both then downgrade their authenticated TLS session to plain TCP and SSL_SHUTDOWN, letting the Relay establish direct s1-s2 forwarding over the already-authorized sockets. In the green serverless-to-serverless (S2S) phase, the assigned client sends a TLS Connection Request over that forwarded socket, and the resulting mTLS handshake gives s1 and s2 a genuine end-to-end secure connection the Relay can no longer read.
